messages:
mira: Hey team, ACME reported a huge p99 spike on Dedicated yesterday during their billing window. They saw p95 ~350ms -> p99 ~1.2s for generation endpoints and are threatening to stop their ramp. Customer: acme-inc, pool: dedicated-acme-eu, tenant_id: t-acme. Can SRE/Oncall triage? :rotating_light:

sam: Looking. Do you have a sample request id or time window?

mira: sample req_id=01H4Y2JZ3, window=2026-02-14T18:12-18:24Z. Graphs attached in thread (p95/p99, queue length).

sam: grabbing traces and metrics now. Initial hunch: scale-up attach latency + cold-GPU init. Will post queries.

diego: I see the spike. Two things pop: 1) attach_time_ms distribution shows large tail (~600-900ms) starting at 18:10. 2) dedicated-acme-eu GPU utilization ~96% and provisioner queue depth jumped. Looks like pool saturated and autoscaler queued requests for attach.

sam: metric snippets I ran (PromQL):
```
# avg attach time over 5m
rate(attach_time_ms_sum{pool="dedicated-acme-eu"}[5m]) / rate(attach_time_ms_count{pool="dedicated-acme-eu"}[5m])
# pending attach requests
sum(scaleup_queue_length{pool="dedicated-acme-eu"})
# GPU util
avg(gpu_utilization_percent{pool="dedicated-acme-eu"})
```

sam: attach queue depth hit 42 concurrent waiting, attach_time tail increased when queue > 8. Also see image pull latencies spiking for one image version: image:redwood/runtime-v2.1.

katie: customer-specific config: min_pool_size=0, burst_mode=true, fallback_model="redwood-small-v1" but fallback policy has a bug (doesn't trigger if pool is saturated).

mira: customer says fallback didn't happen — they remained on heavy model and latencies spiked.

diego: reproducer notes: if pool saturation + min_pool_size=0 + high attach fanout, autoscaler schedules new GPUs but attach path gets queued behind image pulls and cold GPU warmup. Cold GPU init adds ~600ms median when the worker hasn't been used recently.

sam: quick mitigation options I can apply now: 1) increase min_pool_size for dedicated-acme-eu from 0 -> 2, 2) enable prewarm for billing window (start +10m), 3) route small fraction of traffic (10%) to fallback_model via routing override so user impact reduced while we fix fallback bug. Which do we want?

mira: do them all? customer needs fast fix. Authorize if you can.

ops-oncall: I'll patch min_pool_size -> 2, schedule prewarm for next billing window, and set temporary routing override for 20% traffic. Doing in stages to monitor. Patch ETA ~8m. @diego can you look into fallback policy bug?

diego: on it. Root cause: fallback selection checks capacity using an availability flag that is set false when pool utilization >90, but we short-circuit earlier if min_pool_size==0, so fallback is never selected. Simple logic bug in router: `if (min_pool==0) return no_fallback` — bad. I'll open PR to change to: prefer fallback when attach_queue > threshold OR attach_time_mean > X.

diego: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/router/pulls/4721 -> will add metric-driven fallback and a configurable threshold. Requesting review from @katie.

katie: reviewing. Also adding a canary flag so we can toggle metric-driven fallback per-tenant.

infra-bot: deploy started: configs/minpool/dedicated-acme-eu -> 2 (change_id cfg-2026-02-14-17). Rolling update 3 nodes.

sam: quick numbers after min_pool bump + routing override (20% -> fallback): within 6m p95 dropped to ~220ms, p99 down to ~480ms on overall traffic. Attach_queue reduced from peak 42 -> 6. GPU util dropped to ~78%.

mira: customer on call now, feeding numbers. They reported immediate improvement. They want a postmortem and permanent guardrails.

diego: next steps (actionable):
- (A) fix router fallback logic (PR 4721) -> merge + canary (owner: diego)
- (B) add proactive warmup job for dedicated pools with scheduled start (owner: ops-oncall)
- (C) add alert: attach_queue > 10 for >2m -> paging SRE (owner: sam)
- (D) create recommendation for Dedicated tenants: min_pool_size >= 1 during billing windows (doc) (owner: katie)
- (E) investigate image pull cold latencies for runtime-v2.1 and publish mitigation (owner: infra team).

sam: I've opened infra ticket INFRA-3219 to optimize image layering and warm cache for runtime-v2.1. Also added a short-term workaround: keep a small set of warm containers in each region for busy images.

mira: customer asks for timeline for permanent fix to fallback. We should give ETA.

diego: estimate: router fix + tests + canary -> 48-72 hours. Proactive warmup feature -> 5 working days to ship a controlled rollout. Image pull optimizations -> depends (infra triage), initial improvement ETA 7 days.

katie: I'll draft customer communication: explain immediate mitigations we did (min_pool bump + 20% fallback override), outline next steps and timelines.

ops-oncall: monitoring: will keep 15m cadence on p99/p95 dashboards for dedicated-acme-eu for next 48h and will auto-escalate if p99 > 600ms for >10m.

mira: thanks everyone. Please paste final runbook steps + links to PRs/tickets in this thread so I can include in the support postmortem for ACME.

sam: adding runbook snippet:
```
# Emergency runbook - dedicated pool saturation
1) Check `attach_queue_length{pool="<pool>"}` and `gpu_utilization_percent{pool="<pool>"}`
2) If attach_queue > 10 and gpu_util > 90%: bump min_pool_size -> +1 (config change), enable routing override for fallback_model for 10-30% traffic
3) Schedule prewarm job + notify customer
4) Open oncall incident and assign to eng-sre
```

diego: PR/tickets: router PR 4721, INFRA-3219, router bug issue #R-998, config change cfg-2026-02-14-17.

mira: I'll close the customer ticket after I send the comms and attach this thread + runbook. Great work. :tada:
